Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate PROGRAM MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: BS - Environmental Education, Effective Fall 2025 Appendix A The changes in the program seek to make the degree more personalized for the students.
Instead of a prescribed sequence of environmental related courses, student will be able to concentrate in an area of interest utilizing pre-existing environmentally-related courses across the curriculum.
Current 2024-25 curriculum worksheet with narrow options and proposed curriculum worksheet for 2025-26 with flexible course options are both attached.
The comparison highlights the changes.
COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BS – Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Sciences, Effective Fall 2025 Appendix B The Department of Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Sciences, its course offerings, research programs, and degree programs encompass the areas of biomedical and pharmaceutical sciences.

However, upon inception of the bachelor's degree program, the department was hesitant to use the long degree name.
Over time, the exclusion of the biomedical sciences in the name has led to a false perception by students and potential employers that the area is not a focus of the program.
A name change for the program to Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Sciences is being proposed to more fully characterize the program, its offerings, and potential student opportunities.
Biomedical sciences and pharmaceutical sciences have alway been included in the program description.
The changes being made to the program description involve the changing of the degree name.
The addition of health professions programs as an opportunity for graduates has also been added.
Other minor edits to clarify catalog language have been made.

No changes are being made to the curriculum with the exception of dropping ECN 201 from the basic non- science requirements. Students will be able to select any general education A2 course instead, opening the door for students to tailor their academic program to prepare them for their individual career path. For example, pre-health professional students can now take PSY or SOC courses to meet basic requirements for applying to medical, dental, or other health profession schools while students wishing to minor in business could continue to take ECN 201. Edited curriculum sheets are attached to reflect the removal of ECN 201 as a requirement. NEW PROGRAM Minor - Environmental Education, Effective Fall 2025 Appendix C An Environmental Education Minor provides students’ knowledge and skills to facilitate environmental literacy throughout diverse communities. Students who declare a minor must complete at least 18 approved credits: - Ten credits from ENE202 (3), ENE332 (4), and ENE484 (3) - At least 5 additional credits electives within ENE course code - 3 credits from a related a sciences, education, arts, communication, or policy course

Freshman and sophomore year students will identify and describe the influences of social, economic, and cultural identity on access to and engagement in environmental education programs and services, with particular attention to barriers faced by historically underrepresented populations.
In addition, they will learn how development has negatively and positively impacted human relationships with the environment and the developed environment's impacts on the quality of life.
As juniors and seniors they will learn how data science is changing what we know about environmental justice.
They will engage in critical conversations, service learning projects, and research to collect and display data to influence policy makers, and to educate people of all ages and abilities to take positive actions toward a healthy and just society.
An Environmental Education Major at URI supports URI's mission to enrich the lives of students, the community, and beyond through the values of a land and sea grant institution.
Students and faculty will learn and lead together to sustain and improve the conditions for all people locally and across the globe.

The new program will offer unique, creative and interdisciplinary research experiences by embedding students with an education focus into current STEM research and into the work of environmental community partners.
The program will step beyond traditional classroom lectures to engage students in place-based learning experiences and civic involvement projects.
The program will support FOCUS URI, the Strategic Vision for the University priorities.
A few examples of how this program would meet those priorities are: Priority 1 Broaden Our Impact: Goal 1 Contribute to broad and deep impacts on the social, cultural, and economic ecosystems across Rhode Island, the nation, and beyond.
Action 1: Position URI as a vital partner and dynamic leader in solutions-based societal change.
The program aims to create leaders who are capable and confident to promote knowledge and skills to a wide audience to broaden participation in solution-based action.
Action 2: Strengthen relationships with local, state, and federal agencies, as well as community organizations, to identify and implement impactful societal, cultural, and economic initiatives.

The EE program was initiated by community organizations such as the Roger Williams Park Zoo, Save the Bay, and Audubon Society who would like to (1) work more closely with URI on research and outreach (2) would like to have knowledgeable and skilled people apply to their entry level positions and (3) partner as leaders to influence local policy.
Field experiences and internships would develop partnerships with 54 organizational members of the Rhode Island Environmental Association.
In addition, the program would work closely with the North American Association of Environmental Education to become one of the few (less than 5) undergraduate accredited programs in the country.
Action 3: Foster meaningful engagement with alumni, parents, and friends of URI.
Designed into the new program will be a 21st century portfolio assessment system that will include students in a leadership role during a community event day in which students of the program engage alumni, parents, friends, AND future URI generations in learning about research and local impacts on the environment.

Priority 2 Enhance Student Achievement Goal 1 Continuously invigorate the learning environment to reflect active learning; student agency; and contemporary, high-impact learning pedagogies.
The EE program will intentionally break traditional teaching methods by using the forests, the coastlines, and other natural and designed environments as classroom spaces.
The high-impact place-based instruction has potential to attract and retain a more diverse student population and may provide a model and tools for other additional programs to move toward flexible use of classroom space.

1 PROPOSED CHANGE TO OFFICER AND FSEC ELECTIONS Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-7C April 10, 2025 Faculty Senate Meeting (Friendly amendments reflected) Rationale: The original version of this legislation proposed changing the one-year term of one of the four Executive Committee positions to a two-year term, altering the timing of nominating committee formation, and amending how we vote for officers and FSEC members.
The original legislation was proposed at the 3/6/25 meeting; comments made at that meeting and subsequent extended conversations with several senators convinced us to drop the proposed changes to FSEC term lengths and nominating committee dates.
The amended version of the legislation thus only addresses the fact that it is currently possible for senators who attend Faculty Senate meetings in person to vote twice in officer/FSEC elections: once electronically and once in person via anonymous paper ballot.
We propose adopting a standard electronic ballot system for elections held both virtually and in person (hybrid), while maintaining a paper ballot system for elections held only in person.

Election of Officers 5.3 At the meeting(s) at which elections are conducted, nominations from the floor shall be in order.
All candidates may offer a brief oral statement during the meeting regarding their interest and experience.
Paper ballots shall be used in the election for all eligible Senators attending in person and an electronic poll will be administered to all eligible Senators attending remotely.
All ballots/polls shall include a “write-in” option.
A majority of the legal votes cast shall be required to elect. 5.4 The election of officers shall be in accordance with the following procedures: When more than two candidates are nominated for a single office, a candidate shall be declared elected on the first ballot if a majority of the votes cast are received.
If no candidate receives a majority of the first ballot votes, then a run-off election shall be held between the two candidates who have received the highest number of first ballot votes. #21-22-6 For any term of office on the Executive Committee for which two candidates are being elected, a candidate shall be declared elected on the first ballot if a majority of the votes cast are received.
